reader.requirement: At --std 85, when two or more argument-1 values of FUNCTION ORD-MIN are equal and least under the simple-condition rules (algebraic equality across scales and usages, +0 = -0; collating equality including ALSO-equal characters and space extension), the ordinal of the leftmost such argument is returned, for every argument form the 1989 module allows. The witness covers a numeric literal tie and one space-extension tie.

reader.edition-search: As for 1989-RV-A.2.33.4-1: the tie handling is the strict-less update in each runtime body, none of which takes an edition input.

reader.notes: Every carrier keeps the first index and replaces it only on a strictly smaller comparison (c < 0), so the leftmost of equal least values wins; the probes reach the Int128 pair, string and PCS-collation bodies. The aligned Int128 OrdMin in CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs has the same strict update.
